The framework provides built-in upsert m: The framework provides built-in upsert methods that automatically handle both creating new records and updating existing ones. These methods check DynamoDB for existing data and decide whether to create or update, skipping unchanged records for efficiency.
Built-in upsert methods (`upsert`, `upse: Built-in upsert methods (`upsert`, `upsertBulk`, `upsertSetting`, `upsertTenantSetting`) were added in [version 1.1.2](/docs/changelog#v112). In earlier versions, you need to implement custom upsert logic (see [Legacy Upsert Pattern](#legacy-upsert-pattern) below).
Creates or updates a tenant setting. If: Creates or updates a tenant setting. If the setting exists and has changes, it updates. If the setting exists but is unchanged, it returns the existing data without creating a new command. If the setting is deleted, it recreates it.

When the controller is enabled (`enableC: When the controller is enabled (`enableController: true`), the framework provides a unified `/api/master-bulk/` endpoint that can handle both settings and data in a single request. Items are routed based on the presence of `settingCode`:
This item has settingCode → treated as m: This item has settingCode → treated as master data
This item has no settingCode → treated a: This item has no settingCode → treated as master setting

Name of the setting or data: Name of the setting or data
Code of the setting or data: Code of the setting or data

The upsert methods follow these rules:: The upsert methods follow these rules:
**New record**: If no existing record is: **New record**: If no existing record is found, creates a new one (version starts at 0)
**Existing record with changes**: If the: **Existing record with changes**: If the record exists and the input differs, updates it using the existing version number
**Existing record unchanged**: If the re: **Existing record unchanged**: If the record exists and the input is identical, skips the update and returns the existing data
**Deleted record**: If the record exists: **Deleted record**: If the record exists but is marked as deleted (`isDeleted: true`), recreates it using the existing version number

The Master Setting Service implements a: The Master Setting Service implements a four-level hierarchy. Settings cascade from the most specific level toward the most general — `getSetting` returns the first match found:
Baseline values shared by all tenants: Baseline values shared by all tenants
`getSetting` resolves a setting code in: `getSetting` resolves a setting code in this order: **User → Group → Tenant → Common**. If no setting exists at any level, a `NotFoundException` is thrown.
Tenant that holds the common master data: Tenant that holds the common master data (default: `common`)
Opt-in guard for the built-in routes. Se: Opt-in guard for the built-in routes. See [Controller Authorization](#controller-auth)

Database the Prisma client talks to (def: Database the Prisma client talks to (default: detected from the Prisma client). See [Database Provider](#database-provider)
Require a login for reads and system_adm: Require a login for reads and system_admin for writes
Master keys are built from the codes in: Master keys are built from the codes in a request: a setting is stored under `MASTER_SETTING#<code>`, a data row under `<settingCode>#<code>`, and group and user settings under `MASTER_SETTING#GROUP#<groupId>#<code>` and `MASTER_SETTING#USER#<userId>#<code>`. Each of these values must be a single key segment:
It must not contain `#`, the key separat: It must not contain `#`, the key separator. Otherwise the value builds the key of another row; for example the setting code `USER#u1#S1` is a user's personal setting.
It must not contain `@`, the version sep: It must not contain `@`, the version separator of a sort key.
A setting code, and the `settingCode` of: A setting code, and the `settingCode` of master data, must not be `MASTER_SETTING`.
A request that breaks a rule fails with: A request that breaks a rule fails with 400. The rule applies to every setting create and upsert (common, tenant, group, user and bulk), to master data create, upsert and both bulk endpoints, to `getSetting` (`GET /api/master-setting/:code`) and to `MasterDataService.list` (`GET /api/master-data`). Bulk requests validate the keys of every item before the first write.
Rows are changed only through their own: Rows are changed only through their own routes. `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/master-setting/:pk/:sk` (`updateSetting`/`deleteSetting`) accept only setting keys (`MASTER_SETTING#<code>`, plus group and user keys), and `PUT`/`DELETE /api/master-data/:pk/:sk` (`update`/`delete`) reject `MASTER_SETTING#...` keys. Both reject a sort key that contains `@`.
In versions prior to v1.8.0, codes were: In versions prior to v1.8.0, codes were not validated. Core cut a sort key at its last `@`, so a value with one `@`, such as an e-mail address used as a `userId` or code, was silently stored under a truncated, different key, and a code with two or more `@` (for example `X@Y@Z`) could store a row whose key still contains `@` (`MASTER_SETTING#X@Y`). Since v1.8.0 such rows can no longer be read, updated or deleted through the API: find them (a sort key containing `@` in the DynamoDB data table or the RDS master table) and re-create them under a valid key. Master data rows already stored with `#` in their `code` stay readable and can still be updated or deleted by key.
Set `controllerAuth` to protect the buil: Set `controllerAuth` to protect the built-in master routes. Setting it, even as an empty object, turns on `MasterControllerGuard` on `MasterDataController`, `MasterSettingController`, `MasterBulkController`, `MasterAccessController` and the task controller (`/api/tasks`).
A request without a `sub` claim is rejec: A request without a `sub` claim is rejected.
`read` empty or omitted means any logged: `read` empty or omitted means any logged-in user. `write` empty or omitted falls back to `system_admin` only. `system_admin` always passes, and roles resolved from groups count.
`GET` routes and the two `POST .../check: `GET` routes and the two `POST .../check-exist` routes are reads. Every other route is a write.
The tenant named in the request (path ke: The tenant named in the request (path key, `tenantCode` in the body or query, the copy source and targets) must be the caller's tenant, unless the request only reads the common tenant or the caller has a cross-tenant role. Otherwise the guard answers 400 `Invalid tenant code`.
Without `controllerAuth`, the routes sta: Without `controllerAuth`, the routes stay unguarded and `MasterModule` logs a startup warning when the controllers are enabled.
`controllerAuth`, `commonTenantCode`, `e: `controllerAuth`, `commonTenantCode`, `enableCopyTask`, `databaseProvider`, `systemId`, `@MasterAccessResolver()`, `GET /api/master-access`, `assignSystem` and `includeCommon` were added in [version 1.8.0](/docs/changelog#v180). Projects created with `mbc new` from v1.8.0 get an empty `controllerAuth` object, so master writes need `system_admin` until you configure roles.
A caller whose token has no `custom:tena: A caller whose token has no `custom:tenant` claim and who names the common tenant in `x-tenant-code` may get 403 when `commonTenantCode` is not listed in the `COMMON_TENANT_CODES` environment variable, because the tenant-override check of the base `RolesGuard` reads that variable rather than the module option. If you change `commonTenantCode`, add the same value to `COMMON_TENANT_CODES`.
Several products can share master data m: Several products can share master data maintained in one central service. Each master setting can carry a `systemId` that says which product the setting and its data are for, and an optional access resolver grants read and write per system and per setting. Without a resolver, `systemId` is ignored and the services behave as before.
For the full design, the rollout order a: For the full design, the rollout order and publishing changes to SNS per system, see the framework guide [Master data access control and per-system sync](https://github.com/mbc-net/mbc-cqrs-serverless/blob/main/docs/development/master-access-and-sync.md).
`systemId` is stored in `attributes.__sy: `systemId` is stored in `attributes.__systemId` (constant `MASTER_SYSTEM_ATTRIBUTE`, reader `getSystemId(row)`), outside the key, so each setting code has one owner within a tenant. API responses return it as a top-level `systemId` and hide `__systemId` from `attributes`.
A `__systemId` sent by a client in `attr: A `__systemId` sent by a client in `attributes` is always removed, with or without a resolver.
`shared` is reserved for data every syst: `shared` is reserved for data every system receives. A row without a `systemId` counts as `shared`.
A new setting may carry `systemId` in `C: A new setting may carry `systemId` in `CommonSettingDto`, `TenantSettingDto` or a bulk setting item. A setting with the same code as one visible through the tenant-then-common lookup inherits its `systemId`, and a conflicting explicit value is a 400. A tenant-level override of a common setting that has no `systemId` is treated as `shared`.
A data row never accepts `systemId` from: A data row never accepts `systemId` from the client. It takes the value of its effective setting (the tenant's, then the common tenant's).
`systemId` is stored in lower case, cann: `systemId` is stored in lower case, cannot be `*`, and cannot be changed once set.
Group and user settings never store `sys: Group and user settings never store `systemId`; access follows their base setting.
Register exactly one class with `@Master: Register exactly one class with `@MasterAccessResolver()`. The decorator applies `@Injectable()`, so do not add it yourself. Add the class to the providers of a module that is loaded with `MasterModule`. More than one resolver throws at startup.
A grant has `systemId` (or `*`), `settin: A grant has `systemId` (or `*`), `settingCode` (or `*`), `read` and `write`. Write implies read.
With a resolver registered, access is de: With a resolver registered, access is denied by default and grants are a union. If the resolver throws, the request fails.
There is no built-in bypass for `system_: There is no built-in bypass for `system_admin`: the resolver decides, usually by returning `*` grants.
Grants are resolved once per request eve: Grants are resolved once per request event.
`MasterSettingService` and `MasterDataSe: `MasterSettingService` and `MasterDataService` enforce access themselves, so your own routes are checked too. The methods take an options object with `invokeContext` and these optional fields:
Internal callers only, used by copy: Internal callers only, used by copy
A call without `invokeContext` is denied: A call without `invokeContext` is denied with 403, including reads. Server-side code must pass `invokeContext`, or `skipAccessCheck: true` for trusted internal work.
The record's tenant must be the caller's: The record's tenant must be the caller's tenant, a common tenant for a read, or the caller must hold a cross-tenant role.
A caller who is not logged in cannot wri: A caller who is not logged in cannot write, and needs `scope.tenantCode` to read.
The grants must cover the record's `syst: The grants must cover the record's `systemId` (or `shared`) and setting code.
List endpoints add the grants to the Pri: List endpoints add the grants to the Prisma `where`, so pagination and `total` stay correct; no grants means an empty list. A `systemId` in the search only narrows the result. `checkExistCode` checks only the tenant, so a form can warn about a code owned by a system the user cannot see.
`GET /api/master-access` returns `enable: `GET /api/master-access` returns `enabled` and `grants`, so a UI can show or hide actions. Without a resolver, `enabled` is false and `grants` is empty. For a caller who is not logged in, `enabled` is true, `grants` is empty and the resolver is not called. Applications with their own routes can call `MasterAccessService.getAccess` with `invokeContext`.
`MasterSettingService.assignSystem` give: `MasterSettingService.assignSystem` gives the existing untagged rows of a setting code an owning system:
It requires a resolver, and write access: It requires a resolver, and write access on the target system and on `shared`. Without `tenantCode` it covers every tenant and needs a cross-tenant role.
It finds candidate rows in RDS (`system_: It finds candidate rows in RDS (`system_id` is `NULL`), skips a row whose latest command already has a `systemId`, and returns the number of rows it published. Group and user settings are left alone.
It is a migration tool without a built-i: It is a migration tool without a built-in route. Run it before consumers subscribe, and split the work per tenant to stay within the Lambda timeout.
Pass `includeCommon: true` in the search: Pass `includeCommon: true` in the search of `MasterSettingService.list` (`GET /api/master-setting/list`) or `MasterDataService.listByRds` (`GET /api/master-data/list`) to add the common tenant's rows whose code the caller's tenant does not have. It is off by default and works with or without a resolver.
A master data list with `includeCommon`: A master data list with `includeCommon` requires `settingCode`, unless the caller is in the common tenant.
The tenant may hold at most 10,000 match: The tenant may hold at most 10,000 matching rows, soft-deleted rows included; more is a 400. Results are not truncated.
A settings list with `includeCommon` doe: A settings list with `includeCommon` does not merge the common tenant's group and user setting rows.
Access filters on lists read the `system: Access filters on lists read the `system_id` column of the RDS master table. Add a nullable column and write it in the RDS handler:
New projects get both from the template. Projects generated earlier must add them by hand, because `update-scheme.ts` does not change an existing schema or handler. The column is needed only with a resolver. Add the column, update the handler, deploy, and only then register the resolver: with a resolver registered and no `systemId` field on the Prisma `Master` model, the application refuses to start.
With a resolver, `MasterSettingService.c: With a resolver, `MasterSettingService.copy` requires `system_admin` and a write grant whose `systemId` and `settingCode` are both `*`.
For copy, `system_admin` must come from: For copy, `system_admin` must come from the `custom:roles` claim; roles resolved from groups do not count. Copying to another tenant relies on `system_admin` being a cross-tenant role (`CROSS_TENANT_ROLES`, default `system_admin`).
The background copy step runs with `skip: The background copy step runs with `skipAccessCheck`, so it works without user claims. `enableCopyTask` registers it; it defaults to the value of `enableController`.
The master and survey template packages: The master and survey template packages build Prisma search filters for PostgreSQL or MySQL. By default the provider is detected from the Prisma client, falling back to PostgreSQL with a startup warning when it cannot be detected. Set `databaseProvider` to choose it explicitly:
On PostgreSQL, partial-match searches us: On PostgreSQL, partial-match searches use `mode: 'insensitive'`; on MySQL they rely on the default case-insensitive collation. With `registerAsync`, pass `databaseProvider`, `commonTenantCode` and `controllerAuth` statically: the static values override the ones the factory returns.
In versions prior to v1.8.0, name, code: In versions prior to v1.8.0, name, code and keyword searches failed on MySQL, the default database of `mbc new`, because they always sent the PostgreSQL-only `mode: 'insensitive'`. If you patched the dist files to work around this, remove the patch after upgrading.
With `controllerAuth` or an access resol: With `controllerAuth` or an access resolver, copy requires `system_admin` (see [Master Copy Access](#master-copy-access)).
In versions prior to v1.8.0, master copy: In versions prior to v1.8.0, master copy read data from a hard-coded `meltec` tenant instead of the source setting's tenant, and never copied sequences because both keys were built from the target tenant. Since v1.8.0 copy reads the source tenant and copies sequences: a target sequence behind the source jumps to the source's value, and a target that issued numbers in the meantime is never moved back.
Lists master data based on the provided: Lists master data based on the provided search criteria. Without an access resolver, this method does not require an invoke context. With a resolver registered, pass `invokeContext` (or `skipAccessCheck: true`) as the second argument, and rows the caller may not read are left out (see [What the Services Check](#service-checks)).
Narrow the result to one system. Used on: Narrow the result to one system. Used only with an access resolver
Add common tenant rows whose code the te: Add common tenant rows whose code the tenant does not have (see [Include Common Tenant Rows](#include-common))
The endpoint upserts all settings first: The endpoint upserts all settings first and the data rows after, so a data row can use a setting created in the same request. The keys of every item are validated before the first write.
A bulk request is not atomic across sett: A bulk request is not atomic across settings and data. With an access resolver registered, the access checks of the data items run after the settings have been written, so a forbidden data item fails the request with 403 and leaves the settings of the same request written. Since v1.8.0 settings are upserted before data; earlier versions upserted both at once.
Owning system of a new setting (settings: Owning system of a new setting (settings only; used only with an access resolver)
